reason: The toys are repository-owned browser code using existing packages and assets. Delivery uses the already registered GitHub repository, task-manager account, GitHub Actions, and Vercel production project. No new account, spend, runtime service or secret is needed. Control-plane readiness does not prove execution-runner access or a production deploy.

prerequisites.required_setup: GitHub repository quiinthieu/otohime on main, existing git-key-otohime SSH deploy key with repository read/write scope in the registered otohime task-manager repo. Existing account owner quiinthieu and existing cost authority; no new purchase. The control-plane secret-presence probe checks registration only; lease-side git push separately demonstrates write.

Registered otohime software_engineer execution account and fleet worker with Node 22, locked npm install, Chrome for browser checks, and SSH origin access. Existing platform allocation and account/cost authority; scheduler places the work. This capability probe concerns runner placement, not a person launching a machine.

Existing GitHub Actions on quiinthieu/otohime enabled for main pushes, with hosted Ubuntu runner, Node 22, npm registry access, contents:read workflow token and existing deployment configuration. Repository owner quiinthieu has existing Actions cost authority. A control-plane service probe does not establish runner execution.

Existing Vercel otohime production project serving otohime.dev under quiinthieu's account and current cost authority. GitHub Actions VERCEL_TOKEN has deploy access scoped to the project and VERCEL_ORG_ID/VERCEL_PROJECT_ID select it. No new key, project, billing authorization or service is requested; a service probe cannot establish runner credential attachment.
